payload.source_label: Equation (1.9): q_t + f'(q) q_x = 0 is the quasilinear form

contract.statement: For a state q depending on one spatial coordinate and time, the conservation law q_t + ∂_x[f(q)] = 0 is rewritten as q_t + f′(q)q_x = 0, where f′(q) is the flux Jacobian acting on the spatial derivative of the state. This is the rewrite explicitly presented in (1.8)–(1.9) on raw PDF page 25, printed page 3; its classical chain-rule regularity is implicit rather than precisely specified. The vector-valued interpretation comes from raw PDF page 23, printed page 1. The adjacent hyperbolicity observation imports the real-eigenvalue and complete-eigenvector conditions from the opening paragraph of printed page 3. The smoothness and discontinuity discussion on raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, does not license extending this classical rewrite to shock solutions without further interpretation.
assumptions: The starting differential conservation law is q_t(x,t) + ∂_x[f(q(x,t))] = 0. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, (1.8).]

Analyst inference required to interpret the rewrite classically: the relevant derivatives of q and f must exist with sufficient differentiability to apply the chain rule. The rewrite itself gives no exact regularity hypothesis. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, the rewriting sentence and (1.9); raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, Section 1.1.2 supplies related smoothness context.]

The discussion concerns homogeneous, first-order equations with one spatial variable and time. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, introduction to (1.1); raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, opening of Section 1.1.]

The rewrite uses the chain-rule identity ∂_x[f(q(x,t))] = f′(q(x,t))q_x(x,t). This identity is an analyst-explicated mechanism of the displayed rewrite, not an independently numbered source claim. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, (1.8)–(1.9).]

The smooth differential interpretation does not establish the same rewrite for discontinuous solutions: the source expressly discusses the smoothness proviso and shocks in the ensuing subsection. [Raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, Section 1.1.2, opening paragraph.]
quantifiers: Inherited context: q : R × R → R^m is the dependent state, with x the single spatial coordinate and t time; m is the number of components. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, paragraph following (1.1).]

The flux f depends on the state q. Its role in the vector equation and its Jacobian imply a map from admissible states in R^m to R^m; a precise state domain is not specified. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, (1.8)–(1.9) and the flux-Jacobian sentence.]

The displayed equations concern the same state q at the same spatial and temporal arguments; (1.9) suppresses the arguments shown in (1.8). No separate quantified theorem is stated. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, (1.8)–(1.9).]
